analysis.title: US Market Intell Afternoon Briefing, November 10, 2026
key_insights: October CPI was hot again. Core CPI rose 0.30% m/m and headline rose 0.35%, with broad increases (core goods +0.16%, core services +0.34%, food +0.5%). The author says core came in above JPM's 0.23% m/m forecast, with the miss concentrated in services.

The services detail behind the core upside: OER stayed firm at 0.32%, motor vehicle insurance +0.7%, health care +0.3%, recreation services +0.9%. In goods, used vehicles fell 1.2% but household furnishings rose 0.7%, recreation commodities rose 0.7% and new vehicles rose 0.2%.
JPM's core PCE forecast is 0.35% m/m. That would lift the year-over-year rate to 3.3%, the fastest pace since 2023, and the 3-month annualized rate to 3.8%.

Equities closed lower but well off the lows. The selloff was driven by a yield surge after CPI, mostly through real yields rather than inflation expectations. Fed hike bets rose and Friday's PPI is flagged as the next test.

The US Market Intel desk reads the print as unlikely to build support for a 50bp December hike, citing US/Iran resolution pulling commodity prices lower and the AI capex redux easing inflation pressure. It notes the market has begun pricing a higher chance of 50bp, which was not in the narrative before.

The desk's positioning call is to stay constructive on equities and favor ex-AI over AI in the US at least into next week's capital markets event. Lower energy prices are expected to keep Europe outperforming the US.

Fedspeak was hawkish. Waller backs a December hike and is open to 50bp, says energy pass-through is stronger than in the past, and says the minimum is taking back the 3 insurance cuts. Logan says policy is accommodative, more rapid hikes may be needed this winter, and a pause would make sense after two more increases. Bowman flagged risk of a large equity valuation correction and financial stability risk if AI returns disappoint.

Joe Lupton argues the current productivity boom reflects capital deepening and factor utilization more than technology gains, so true AI gains will take longer. This supports JPM's call for a cyclical rise in hiring, sticky inflation and higher rates.

The NFIB small business survey showed the hiring sub-index rising again (it leads NFP by 1-3 months). 86% of owners who hired or tried to hire found few or no qualified applicants, compensation is above historical averages, and 37% plan to raise prices, the highest since July 2022.

Technicals (Jason Hunter): the rebounds in SOX and NASDAQ 100 are stalling below resistance with no capitulation signal. Sentiment gauges are in the low-to-mid 30% bulls, not deeply oversold. SOX resistance is 10445-10895 and 11600-12000, NDX resistance is 28004 and 28750-30000, and SPX first medium-term support is 7235-7330.

Desk flow color: NVDA supply is accelerating on uncertainty around Jensen Huang and a reported Information article on China chip sales, with money reallocating to hyperscalers. Info Tech is the largest sell sector, NVDA fell 6.5% and accounted for about a third of the NDX decline, and value traded was about 50% below Thursday's drawdown.
Ben Kussin says the bar for re-risking is high and investors are in 'job security mode'. IPO news tried to drive an early momentum bid, but CPI and Waller/Logan outweighed it.

Delta-one desks: high short interest, high beta and levered names led the declines (RTY below SPY). The AI rotation trade is described as late-stage, with S&P ex-AI outperforming the S&P 500 by more than 5%. Manish Sinha sees ex-AI carrying more downside risk than the index if rates rise or AI demand slows.

Commodities: dollar strength hit metals. Copper fell 1.6%, aluminium fell 1.8% on SHFE selling with open interest up 15%, and gold and silver were among the biggest losers (gold -261bps to $4,032, silver -355bps to $51.52).

Synchrony (via a broker conference): management does not see a 2027 recession and frames higher charge-offs as manageable. The author's view is that fee or rate caps remain the headwind, and at 7x NTM EPS the stock is not dirt cheap until about 5x.

market_movers.rationale: TMT desk sees supply accelerating as Jensen Huang-related outcomes are priced, after a reported Information article on China chip sales. NVDA fell 6.5% and drove about a third of the NDX decline, with money rotating to hyperscalers.
Fins desk says management's credit and growth commentary sounds rational, but fee or rate caps would override it. Shares trade at 7x NTM EPS and the author wants about 5x before calling it cheap.

sector_views.rationale: Market Intel favors ex-AI over AI into next week's capital markets event, while the factors desk warns ex-AI may carry more downside if rates rise or AI demand slows.
TMT desk favors the hyperscaler setup on higher data center build costs and possible capex growth moderation in 2028 and beyond. The only headwind named is positioning, which is not as clean.
Delta-one desk shows homebuilders lagging the market (-1.9 sigma) and proposes a pair favoring repair and remodel as mortgage lock-in favors remodeling over moving.
Lower energy prices are expected to keep EU equities outperforming the US.

earnings_insights: SYF (Synchrony) at a broker conference: management sees credit as seasonal and resilient, does not see a 2027 recession, and calls higher charge-offs manageable. Near-term loan growth is modest, and next year's EPS growth is expected from NII growth, operating leverage and buybacks. Shares trade at 7x NTM EPS (estimate basis, per the author).
Infineon forecasts strong 2027 growth on data-centre demand (Reuters news link, no figures given in this report).
Earnings calendar: Nov 10 includes CRWV, QBTS, RGTI, TDG. Nov 11 includes CTVA and VYLR. Nov 12 includes AMAT and CSCO. Nov 13 includes PARA.

OER 0.32%, motor vehicle insurance 0.7%, recreation services 0.9%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since July 2022, pointing to persistent inflation.
Yields surged after CPI, mostly via real yields. 10Y bonds were -2.6 sigma on the day per the thematics desk.

macro_indicators.reading: Waller open to 50bp hike in December. Next FOMC Dec 9
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market now prices a higher probability of a 50bp hike, while Market Intel thinks CPI alone is unlikely to win broad support for it.

trade_ideas.description: Long Repair & Remodel (JPUXRR Index) vs short Homebuilders (JP2HOME Index)
trade_ideas.rationale: The pair is beginning to break out as mortgage lock-in continues to favor remodeling over moving.

trade_ideas.description: Favor US equities ex-AI over AI into next week's capital markets event, stay constructive on equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Hot CPI is not seen as supporting a 50bp hike, lower energy prices and AI capex redux ease inflation pressure.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher rates and an AI-driven demand slowdown could hit ex-AI harder than the index (factors desk).

trade_ideas.description: Favor hyperscalers over NVDA and chip suppliers
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher data center build costs and potential moderation in capex growth in 2028 and beyond favor the hyperscaler setup.
trade_ideas.risk: Positioning in hyperscalers is not nearly as clean.

trade_ideas.description: Buy VWO as the ETF desk's best call for those looking to raise cash, with decent size facilitated
trade_ideas.rationale: Real-money demand skewing the ETF desk to buy on the pad.

risk_factors: Further rate hikes, including a possible 50bp December move, with Friday's PPI as the next data risk.
Real-yield surge with the 10Y near 5% pressuring equity valuations.
Bowman's flagged risk of a large equity valuation correction and financial stability risk if AI returns disappoint.
Fee or rate caps on card lenders (SYF) and consumer credit strain, with credit card debt at a record $1.29 trillion.
Nvidia China-related legal and headline uncertainty and accelerating supply in NVDA.
Global macro funds as a positioning risk for US stocks.
Sticky inflation from services, wages and small business pricing intentions.
A slowdown in AI demand weighing on economic demand and ex-AI names.
charts_described: Small Biz Survey Hiring Index vs NFP (1-month lagged): the text states the hiring sub-index tends to precede NFP moves by 1-3 months, no chart levels are given in the text.
vol_and_positioning: ETF desk: shorts appeared to get over their skis and were stopped out, with long-seller flow in SOXS (triple short semiconductors) hitting bids at -21% on the session, showing two-way stress. Real-money buyers in VWO, XLC, XLE and GDX/GDXJ, with the desk a seller of VEA and VTI.
Pure-play AI ETF wrapper demand facilitated in recent weeks has stayed invested, with no supply seen from real-money accounts that added.
Info Tech is the largest sell sector in the TMT room, led by NVDA and memory. Volumes are about 20% above the 5-day average. Comm Services, Discretionary and Health Care are buy sectors.
Short Interest Factor was -1.5 sigma, and high short interest, high beta, high leverage names led declines (RTY below SPY).
Hunter notes DSI and AAII sentiment are at low-to-mid 30% bulls, not the extreme readings that mark capitulation.
Sinha says the S&P ex-AI index currently realizes 1-2 points less volatility than the S&P 500, which may offer more downside protection at this stage.
Global macro funds are flagged as the next positioning risk for US stocks (Bloomberg news link).
Value traded was about 50% below the Thursday drawdown. Kussin says the bar for re-risking is high.
geopolitical: US/Iran resolution is cited as pulling commodity prices lower, and oil eased to two-month lows as the US downplayed further Iran strikes.
Reported Information article alleging Jensen Huang knew chips were being sold illegally to China shell companies, adding to Nvidia's China problem.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027 (NBC link).
APEC Economic Leaders Meeting in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19, the US government funding deadline on Dec 11, and the G20 Summit in Miami on Dec 15-16 are listed as political catalysts.

tension_points.bull_case: Market Intel says the CPI print is unlikely to win much support for a 50bp December hike, citing US/Iran resolution lowering commodity prices and the AI capex redux reducing inflation pressure. Equities stay constructive.
tension_points.bear_case: Waller backs a December hike and is open to 50bp, says energy pass-through is stronger than in the past, and Logan says more rapid hikes may be needed this winter. JPM economists see core PCE at 0.35% m/m.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot PPI on Friday (Nov 13) or further hawkish Fedspeak, which would raise the odds of a 50bp December move ahead of the Dec 9 FOMC.

tension_points.bull_case: Market Intel favors ex-AI over AI into next week's capital markets event, and S&P ex-AI has outperformed the S&P 500 by more than 5% as the rotation continues.
tension_points.bear_case: Factors desk says ex-AI is exposed to higher interest rates and an AI-driven demand slowdown, so its downside risk may exceed the S&P 500's, while the index realizes 1-2 points less volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's capital markets event passing, or rates rising further, which the factors desk says would hit ex-AI harder.
